risks.note: MGL's own risk table names this first. Marketing exclusivity in a PNGRB geographical area is time-limited, so the structural moat MGL claims ('Infrastructure Exclusivity and Reach') has an expiry that the Company itself flags. Stated mitigation: infrastructure expansion and promotional strategies targeting high-potential customer segments, digital loyalty programmes, WhatsApp-based engagement, and diversification into LNG (MLPL JV), EV (3EV stake), CBG and battery storage.
risks.risk: Market and Competitive Risk — loss of market share due to alternate fuels and end of exclusivity rights

risks.note: MGL buys a regulated-price domestic pool (APM, NWG, HPHT) plus market-linked RLNG, and prices CNG/PNG against LPG, FO and LDO benchmarks; a cut in APM allocation forces the mix toward Henry Hub / Brent-linked term RLNG and spot RLNG, compressing the spread. Stated mitigation: monthly CNG and PNG pricing reviews and a diversified gas sourcing portfolio including APM, HPHT, Henry Hub-linked and Brent-linked term contracts. Sibling bundles record the FY26 realisation of this risk — reduced APM allocation and Q4 FY26 higher-cost spot RLNG procurement pressuring margins.
risks.risk: Gas sourcing, allocation and price risk — APM allocation cuts, alternate-fuel-linked pricing pressure and currency exposure ('Monetary Risk')

risks.note: BRSR material issue #2, classified 'Risk'. 'Pipeline & compressor infrastructure is backbone of CGD industry. Gas being inflammable and a necessity of life; where any compromise in asset integrity or ineffective incident management can lead to gas leakage, fire, explosion, injuries, operational disruption, and regulatory non-compliance.' Financial implication is explicitly open-ended: 'Negative implication would depend upon the extent of damage and /or period for which gas supply is discontinued.' Mitigation: Asset Integrity Policy and Integrity Management Plan, risk audit framework, pipeline surveillance and defect assessment & repair policy, Management of Change and Non-Routine Operation procedures, ERDMP mock drills. The Process Risk row adds QRA and HAZOP studies, looped pipeline architecture, multiple CGS, a 24x7 emergency crew and an ICCP system.
risks.risk: Asset integrity and critical incident management — gas leakage, fire, explosion, injuries and supply discontinuity

risks.note: BRSR material issue #6. MGL 'caters to a large number of domestic customers'; gas is received at a CGS at around 19 bar and stepped down so that at cooking stoves the pressure is just 21 millibar. The risk is that engineering controls do not reach the last metre — 'lack of awareness about product usage, hazards etc. at the end of customers could pose significant risk of accidents.' Stated financial implication: negative, 'due to consequential costs and reputational damage'. Mitigation: awareness via invoices, mailers, website, newsprint advertisements and registration camps, regular safety awareness sessions at CNG stations and in PNG housing societies, and an after-sales service mechanism.
risks.risk: End-use safety — customer-side accidents from lack of awareness about product usage and hazards

risks.note: BRSR material issue #10, classified 'Risk & Opportunity'. This is the existential structural risk for a single-fuel distributor: 'Shifts in the energy landscape from electrification, renewable adoption, and technological changes may influence long-term natural gas demand, requiring business adaptability.' MGL states the consequence explicitly — 'Delayed adaptation may result in demand risk and under-utilized assets' — which is the risk that its pipeline and station capex becomes stranded. Mitigation is monitoring transition trends, evaluating diversification opportunities and operational efficiency.
risks.risk: Energy transition and business-model resilience — electrification and renewable adoption eroding long-term natural gas demand

risks.note: BRSR material issue #7 plus a dedicated row in the MD&A risk table, and the Directors' Report states the Board 'continues to place enhanced focus on data protection and cyber security risks'. 'A large amount of personal data is captured for operational reasons, particularly in household customer category.' Notably several controls are stated as NOT yet in place: Data Loss Prevention, Mobile Device Management and a Security Operations Centre 'are in the process of implementation'; masking of customer mobile numbers and email IDs 'is being implemented'; a Privacy Management Tool for DPDP compliance 'is being evaluated'. In place: Data Privacy Framework based on DPDP Act 2023, ERP role-based access control, periodic security audits including vulnerability assessment and penetration testing, AI-powered C4i Platform, vendor risk assessments and Data Protection Impact Assessments.
risks.risk: Cybersecurity and data privacy — breach of customer or operational data under the DPDP Act 2023

risks.note: BRSR material issue #9, 'Risk & Opportunity'. Structurally acute because MGL's network is concentrated in Mumbai and coastal Maharashtra. 'Physical climate risks may increase maintenance and repair costs, resulting in negative financial implications', offset by positioning as a transition-fuel provider supporting 'access to sustainable finance'. Mitigation: asset protection measures, business continuity plan and monitoring of climate-related risks.
risks.risk: Climate adaptation and physical climate risk — flooding, heavy rainfall and heatwaves affecting assets and service continuity

risks.note: Evidenced rather than labelled: a third party damaged a GAIL pipeline inside the RCF premises at Trombay, cutting the 18-inch feeder to the Wadala CGS which handles ~2.2 mmscmd of daily drawls, and disrupting supply across Mumbai, its suburbs and parts of Thane and Navi Mumbai (BACK-FILLED from the Manufactured Capital spread in strategy_outlook.txt). MGL's own GHG mitigation text also names 'third party damages' as a monitored event class. The looped network linking CGS Wadala, Mahape, Taloja and Savroli is the stated mitigation, which is also an admission of how concentrated the receiving nodes are.
risks.risk: Third-party damage and single-node supply concentration — dependence on GAIL feeder pipelines into a small number of City Gate Stations
